form.zh: 乐府诗（七言为主的杂言古诗）
form.en: yuefu song (an old-style poem of mixed line lengths, mostly seven characters)

text_note.zh: 课本和通行本与这里用的古籍原文有几处不同：通行本作“金樽”“倾耳听”“沽取”，原文作“金尊”“侧耳听”“酤取”。“樽”和“尊”、“沽”和“酤”意思相同。“但愿长醉不复醒”一句，有的版本作“不愿醒”或“不用醒”，这里保留“不复醒”。
text_note.en: The commonly taught text differs from the source text in a few places. It has jīn zūn (wine cup), qīng ěr tīng (tilt your ear) and gū qǔ (buy wine), where the source uses older characters or cè ěr tīng (turn your ear). The meanings are the same. In the line about staying drunk, some editions end with bù yuàn xǐng (unwilling to wake) or bù yòng xǐng (no need to wake); this text keeps bù fù xǐng (never wake again).

readings.zh: 这里是“头发”的意思，读 fà，不读 fā。
readings.en: Here it means hair, so it is read fà, not fā.

readings.zh: 这里是“早晨”的意思，读 zhāo，不读 cháo。
readings.en: Here it means morning, so it is read zhāo, not cháo.

readings.zh: 这里是“回来”的意思，一般读 huán。也有人读 hái，当“还会”讲。
readings.en: Here it means to come back, and is usually read huán. Some read it hái, meaning "will still".
Wéi lè means to make merry, so it is read wéi.

readings.zh: “将进酒”的“将”是“请”的意思，读 qiāng。
readings.en: In the title phrase qiāng jìn jiǔ, this character means "please" and is read qiāng.
Wèi wǒ means for me, so it is read wèi.

readings.zh: “斗”是古代量酒的器具，读 dǒu，不读 dòu。
readings.en: Here it is an old measure for wine, read dǒu, not dòu.
Hé wèi means why, so it is read wèi.

readings.zh: “将出”是“拿出去”，这里读 jiāng，和第十三句的 qiāng 不同。
readings.en: Jiāng chū means to take out. Here it is read jiāng, unlike the qiāng in line thirteen.

glosses.zh: 君不见：你没有看见吗？乐府诗里常用的开头，用来引起大家注意。君，你。
glosses.en: jūn bù jiàn: haven't you seen? A common opening in old songs, to make the listener pay attention. Jūn means you.

glosses.zh: 天上来：黄河从很高的地方流下来，远远看去，好像是从天上来的。
glosses.en: tiān shàng lái: the Yellow River comes down from very high land, so from far away it looks as if it falls from the sky.

glosses.zh: 不复回：不再回来。复，再。
glosses.en: bù fù huí: never comes back. Fù means again.

glosses.zh: 高堂：高大的厅堂。一说指父母。
glosses.en: gāo táng: a tall hall in a house. Another reading says it means one's parents.

glosses.zh: 悲白发：对着镜子，为满头白发而伤心。
glosses.en: bēi bái fà: to look in the mirror and feel sad about one's white hair.

glosses.zh: 青丝：黑头发。
glosses.en: qīng sī: black hair (literally, dark silk threads).

glosses.zh: 暮成雪：到了傍晚就白得像雪。早晚之间，说的是人老得很快。
glosses.en: mù chéng xuě: by evening it is white as snow. Morning to evening stands for how fast a person grows old.

glosses.zh: 得意：称心如意，高兴的时候。
glosses.en: dé yì: when things go as you wish, when you are happy.

glosses.zh: 须尽欢：应该尽情地快乐。须，应当。
glosses.en: xū jìn huān: should enjoy it to the full. Xū means should.

glosses.zh: 金樽：精美的酒杯。樽，古代盛酒的器具。
glosses.en: jīn zūn: a fine wine cup. Zūn is an old vessel for wine.

glosses.zh: 空对月：空着酒杯对着月亮，意思是不喝酒，白白浪费了好时光。
glosses.en: kōng duì yuè: an empty cup facing the moon, that is, wasting a lovely night without drinking.

glosses.zh: 我材：我的才能。材，同“才”。
glosses.en: wǒ cái: my talent. Here cái is the same as the word for talent.

glosses.zh: 千金：很多很多的钱。
glosses.en: qiān jīn: a thousand pieces of gold, a great deal of money.

glosses.zh: 烹：煮。
glosses.en: pēng: to cook, to boil.

glosses.zh: 且为乐：姑且作乐，先痛快一下。且，暂且。
glosses.en: qiě wéi lè: let us just make merry for now. Qiě means for the time being.

glosses.zh: 会须：应当，正应该。
glosses.en: huì xū: really ought to.

glosses.zh: 三百杯：说喝很多酒，是夸张的说法。
glosses.en: sān bǎi bēi: three hundred cups, a playful way of saying a great many.

glosses.zh: 岑夫子：指岑勋，李白的朋友。夫子，对男子的尊称。
glosses.en: cén fū zǐ: Master Cen, that is, Cen Xun, a friend of Li Bai. Fūzǐ is a polite way to address a man.

glosses.zh: 丹丘生：指元丹丘，李白的好朋友，是一位隐士。生，对读书人的称呼。
glosses.en: dān qiū shēng: Danqiu, that is, Yuan Danqiu, a close friend of Li Bai who lived as a hermit. Shēng is a way to address a scholar.

glosses.zh: 将进酒：请喝酒吧。将，请。这也是这首诗的题目，本是汉代乐府的旧曲名。
glosses.en: qiāng jìn jiǔ: please drink. Qiāng means please. This is also the poem's title, the name of an old Han dynasty song.

glosses.zh: 杯莫停：酒杯不要停下来。
glosses.en: bēi mò tíng: don't let the cups stop.

glosses.zh: 与君：给你们，为你们。
glosses.en: yǔ jūn: for you all.

glosses.zh: 倾耳听：侧着耳朵认真听。
glosses.en: qīng ěr tīng: to tilt your ear and listen closely.

glosses.zh: 钟鼓：富贵人家吃饭时要敲钟打鼓奏乐，这里代指富贵的生活。
glosses.en: zhōng gǔ: bells and drums. Rich families had music played at their meals, so this stands for a life of wealth.

glosses.zh: 馔玉：像玉一样精美的饭菜。馔，饭食。
glosses.en: zhuàn yù: food as fine as jade. Zhuàn means food.

glosses.zh: 不足贵：不值得看重。
glosses.en: bù zú guì: not worth valuing.

glosses.zh: 长醉：一直醉着。
glosses.en: cháng zuì: to stay drunk for a long time.

glosses.zh: 圣贤：圣人和贤人，品德和才能都很高的人。
glosses.en: shèng xián: sages and worthy people, those of great virtue and talent.

glosses.zh: 寂寞：冷清，被人冷落，默默无闻。
glosses.en: jì mò: lonely, left out, soon forgotten.

glosses.zh: 饮者：喝酒的人。
glosses.en: yǐn zhě: drinkers.

glosses.zh: 陈王：指三国时魏国的曹植，他被封为陈王，很有才华。
glosses.en: chén wáng: the Prince of Chen, that is, Cao Zhi of the Three Kingdoms period, a very gifted poet.

glosses.zh: 宴平乐：在平乐观摆酒宴。平乐观，汉代洛阳的一座宫观。曹植写过“归来宴平乐，美酒斗十千”。
glosses.en: yàn píng lè: to hold a feast at the Pingle Hall, a palace building in Luoyang from Han times. Cao Zhi once wrote of coming home to feast at Pingle with wine at ten thousand coins a measure.

glosses.zh: 斗酒十千：一斗酒值十千钱，形容酒非常贵。
glosses.en: dǒu jiǔ shí qiān: one measure of wine cost ten thousand coins, meaning very costly wine.

glosses.zh: 恣欢谑：尽情地欢笑玩乐。恣，放纵、任意；谑，开玩笑。
glosses.en: zì huān xuè: to laugh and joke as much as one likes. Zì means freely; xuè means to joke.

glosses.zh: 主人：请客的人，这里是李白自称。
glosses.en: zhǔ rén: the host. Here Li Bai means himself.

glosses.zh: 何为：为什么。
glosses.en: hé wèi: why.

glosses.zh: 言少钱：说钱不够。
glosses.en: yán shǎo qián: to say there is not enough money.

glosses.zh: 径须：只管，干脆。
glosses.en: jìng xū: just go ahead and.

glosses.zh: 沽取：买来。沽，买酒。
glosses.en: gū qǔ: to go and buy. Gū means to buy wine.

glosses.zh: 酌：倒酒，喝酒。
glosses.en: zhuó: to pour wine, to drink.

glosses.zh: 五花马：名贵的好马。一说马的鬃毛剪成五瓣花的样子，一说马身上有五种颜色的花纹。
glosses.en: wǔ huā mǎ: a fine, costly horse. One reading says its mane was trimmed into five petals; another says its coat had patterns of five colours.

glosses.zh: 千金裘：值千金的皮衣。裘，皮衣。
glosses.en: qiān jīn qiú: a fur coat worth a thousand gold pieces. Qiú is a fur coat.

glosses.zh: 呼儿：叫来年轻的仆人。
glosses.en: hū ér: to call the young servant.

glosses.zh: 将出：拿去。将，拿。
glosses.en: jiāng chū: to take out. Jiāng means to take.

glosses.zh: 尔：你们。
glosses.en: ěr: you all.

glosses.zh: 销：消除，解除。
glosses.en: xiāo: to melt away, to get rid of.

glosses.zh: 万古愁：无穷无尽的忧愁，从古到今人人都有的愁。
glosses.en: wàn gǔ chóu: endless sorrow, the sorrow people have felt since ancient times.

translation.zh: 你没看见吗？黄河的水像从天上奔下来，
translation.en: Haven't you seen the Yellow River's waters pour down as if from the sky,

translation.zh: 一路奔流到大海，再也不会回来。
translation.en: rushing on to the sea and never coming back?

translation.zh: 你没看见吗？高堂上的人对着明镜，为白发伤心，
translation.en: Haven't you seen people in tall halls grieve at the white hair in their bright mirrors,

translation.zh: 早上还是黑亮的头发，到傍晚就白得像雪。
translation.en: hair black as silk at dawn, white as snow by dusk?

translation.zh: 人生得意的时候，就应该尽情欢乐，
translation.en: When life goes your way, enjoy it to the full;

translation.zh: 不要让金杯空空地对着明月。
translation.en: don't let your golden cup stand empty under the moon.

translation.zh: 老天生下我的才能，一定有用处，
translation.en: Heaven gave me my talents, and they must be of use;

translation.zh: 千金花光了，还会再回来。
translation.en: spend a thousand pieces of gold, and they will come back again.

translation.zh: 煮羊杀牛，暂且痛快作乐吧，
translation.en: Cook the lamb, kill the ox, and let us make merry for now;

translation.zh: 一喝就应该喝它三百杯。
translation.en: once we start, we ought to drink three hundred cups.

translation.zh: 岑夫子啊，
translation.en: Master Cen,

translation.zh: 丹丘生啊，
translation.en: my friend Danqiu,

translation.zh: 请喝酒吧，
translation.en: please, drink up,

translation.zh: 酒杯不要停下来。
translation.en: don't let the cups stop.

translation.zh: 我给你们唱一首歌，
translation.en: Let me sing you a song;

translation.zh: 请你们为我侧耳细听。
translation.en: please lend me your ears and listen.

translation.zh: 敲钟打鼓、山珍海味的富贵生活，不值得看重，
translation.en: Bells, drums and food fine as jade are not worth prizing;

translation.zh: 我只希望一直醉着，不再醒来。
translation.en: all I want is to stay drunk and never wake again.

translation.zh: 自古以来，圣人贤人都冷冷清清，被人忘记，
translation.en: Since ancient times the sages and the wise have been lonely and forgotten;

translation.zh: 只有会喝酒的人留下了名声。
translation.en: only the drinkers have left their names behind.

translation.zh: 当年陈王曹植在平乐观大摆酒宴，
translation.en: Long ago the Prince of Chen held a feast at Pingle Hall,

translation.zh: 一斗酒值十千钱，大家尽情说笑。
translation.en: wine at ten thousand coins a measure, laughing and joking as he pleased.

translation.zh: 我这个主人为什么要说钱不够呢？
translation.en: Why should I, the host, say I am short of money?

translation.zh: 只管去买酒来，和你们对饮。
translation.en: Just go and buy more wine, and drink with you.

translation.zh: 名贵的五花马，
translation.en: My fine dappled horse,

translation.zh: 价值千金的皮衣，
translation.en: my fur coat worth a thousand gold,

translation.zh: 叫孩子拿去换美酒，
translation.en: call the boy to take them and trade them for good wine,

translation.zh: 我要和你们一起，消掉这万古的忧愁。
translation.en: and with you I'll drown the sorrows of ten thousand ages.

background.zh: “将进酒”是汉代乐府的旧题目，意思是“请喝酒”。这首诗一般认为写于唐玄宗天宝年间，一说是天宝十一载（752年）前后。那时李白离开长安已经好几年，在朝廷里的抱负没有实现。他和朋友岑勋一起，到元丹丘的山中住处做客，三人喝酒唱歌，李白借着酒兴写下了这首诗。写作的具体年份，学者说法不一。
background.en: Qiang Jin Jiu, "please drink", was the title of an old Han dynasty song. The poem is usually dated to the Tianbao years of Emperor Xuanzong; one view puts it around 752. By then Li Bai had left the capital, Chang'an, several years before, and his hopes of serving at court had come to nothing. With his friend Cen Xun he visited Yuan Danqiu at his home in the hills. The three drank and sang, and in that mood Li Bai wrote this poem. Scholars do not agree on the exact year.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），唐代大诗人，被人称为“诗仙”。他性格豪放，爱喝酒，爱游山玩水，诗写得像天马行空一样自由。他曾在长安为皇帝写诗，但不被真正重用，不久就离开了。这首诗里那种狂放和自信，又带着说不出的苦闷，正是李白的样子。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762) was a great Tang poet, often called the Immortal of Poetry. He was bold and free, loved wine and loved to roam the mountains, and his poems fly as freely as a heavenly horse. He once wrote poems for the emperor in Chang'an, but was never given real work and soon left. The wild confidence in this poem, mixed with a sadness he cannot quite name, is Li Bai through and through.

appreciation.zh: 诗一开头就像打开了闸门：黄河从天上冲下来，一去不回；镜子里的黑发，一天就变成白雪。时间和生命走得这样快，怎么办？李白的回答是：趁着高兴，尽情喝酒！接着他大声说“天生我材必有用，千金散尽还复来”，这是对自己满满的信心。中间他喊朋友的名字劝酒，像真的在酒桌上一样热闹。可是热闹里藏着苦：他说圣贤都寂寞，只有喝酒的人留下名字，其实是在说有才能却不被重用的不平。最后他连好马和皮衣都要拿去换酒，只为消掉“万古愁”。读这首诗，你能感到一股像黄河一样奔腾的气势，也能感到气势下面深深的忧愁。
appreciation.en: The poem opens like a floodgate. The Yellow River crashes down from the sky and never returns. Black hair in the mirror turns white as snow in a single day. Time and life run away so fast, so what should we do? Li Bai's answer: while you are happy, drink to the full! Then he cries out that heaven gave him talent for a reason, and money spent will come back. That is pure self-belief. In the middle he calls his friends by name and urges them to drink, as lively as a real party. But under the noise there is pain. When he says the sages were lonely and only drinkers are remembered, he is really protesting that gifted people like him go unused. At the end he would even trade his fine horse and fur coat for wine, just to wash away a sorrow as old as time. Reading it, you feel a force rushing like the Yellow River, and under that force, a deep sadness.
